Quick sketch — high level first, details to put into the playbook: 

1) Traffic classification and priority- interactive (low token count, < 1k tokens), scheduled batch (longer tail)- For interactive: guarantee p50/p95 using small-priority window tokens, for batch: allow preemption above baseline

2) Admission policy- Maintain a token-bucket per ingress LB with a global controller that tracks aggregate GPU utilization and KV cache hit rates- Admission checks in order: capacity token, KV warmness, request priority. If capacity token exhausted, check fallback model variant (quantized) before rejecting

3) Warm-pool choreography- Pre-warm N=2 reserved GPU nodes per AZ for primary model; ramp additional N based on rolling-avg QPS over 60s windows- Warmup sequence: model artifact load -> KV pre-populate with recent prefixes -> dry-run short prompts to fill KV -> mark node InService

4) Burst absorption strategy- Soft-queue for <60s with progress meter vs hard-drop after 120s; prioritized eviction of batch tasks during spike

Sizing notes (back-of-envelope)
- With profile in spreadsheet, interactive baseline of 1200 rps maps to ~8 A100-equivalent GPUs with 30% headroom for KV miss variability- To absorb 9k rps for 15 minutes we need a combination of warm pool + short-term burst fleet: warm pool ~8 GPUs + on-demand burst of ~20 GPUs (quantized variants) depending on model latency targets

Next: I’ll formalize these numbers into a small workbook and link the network path implications.

-Vivek

ACME team — attaching the short playbook and a conservative commitment matrix (see attached "admission_control_playbook.md"). Key callouts below: 

- Warm-pool thresholds: start accepting interactive traffic once KV hit-rate >= 55% and node free GPU utilization < 60%. We recommend 55% as a balance (higher threshold reduces cold-start latency variance but increases warm-pool size).
- Quantized fallback latency: expect median ~1.15x, p95 ~1.35x compared to FP16 baseline for the same batch sizes in our lab runs (details in workbook).
- Commitment matrix (summary): Sustained 1200 rps with p95 latency <= 220ms (with 8 reserved GPUs + 30% headroom); Burst absorption to 9k rps for 15m: best-effort graceful degradation with prioritization + quantized fallback; guaranteed baseline of 3x sustained bursts with progressive shedding beyond that.
- Network notes: keep the primary model traffic within AZ; use cross-AZ only for analytics replication; recommend an LB scaling plan that adds nodes proactively when ingress QPS exceeds 70% of node capacity.

Next steps:
1) ACME to confirm spike distribution per endpoint (Samir noted endpoint A ~70%).
2) Redwood to produce the final workbook (numbers finalized) and an ops runbook (we will include rollback and circuit-breaker thresholds).

Attachments: admission_control_playbook.md, acme_throughput_targets_workbook.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll schedule a 30-min review with the SRE/infra hosts and product owners for tomorrow morning.
